title: A Quantum Algorithm for the Radical of a Lie Algebra: Kernel Projection and Conditioning
abstract: Every finite-dimensional real or complex Lie algebra has a largest solvable ideal, its radical. In the compact dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) of a closed quantum system, this radical is the center; projecting onto it isolates directions that commute with the supplied algebra. With sparse Lie-bracket data and a known spectral gap, we construct a quantum circuit that approximately encodes this coefficient-space projector. The general construction combines the derived-algebra map with the Killing form, whereas compactness makes the Killing form alone sufficient. This distinction matters for numerical sensitivity, and our main theorem gives its exact law under an invariant-orthonormal basis adapted to the center and semisimple part. In a compact real algebra with a nonzero semisimple part, the condition number of the general operator is the three-halves power of the Killing-form condition number on that part. The compact projector in turn yields a bounded-error test for whether the center is trivial, provided that any nonzero center has at least a stated minimum dimension. This gives a controlled test for internal conserved directions in compact quantum dynamics.
summary: This work presents a quantum algorithm to compute the radical of a Lie algebra, which corresponds to finding conserved directions in the dynamics of a closed quantum system. By encoding the necessary projector into a quantum circuit, it offers a resource-efficient method to test whether the system's center is trivial. This is significant for understanding the internal symmetries and conserved quantities governing quantum evolution.
main_problem: The paper develops a quantum algorithm to find the radical (largest solvable ideal) of a Lie algebra, particularly focusing on the compact case where the radical is the center.
main_result: It constructs a quantum circuit that approximates the coefficient-space projector onto the radical, providing a controlled test for internal conserved directions in compact quantum dynamics.
method: The approach uses quantum linear algebra techniques, specifically constructing a quantum circuit that implements a kernel projection, leveraging tools like QSVT to filter out zero-singular-value components.
model_or_system: The system is the Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA) of a closed quantum system, which is treated as a compact Lie algebra generated by skew-Hermitian matrices within the unitary algebra u(N).
key_observables: The radical (center) of the Lie algebra, the coefficient-space projector, and the condition number ($\kappa$) of the associated operators.
important_parameters: The input requires certified metadata bounds on structure constants ($F, 	ext{sad}_j, 	ext{sint}$) and an error tolerance ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The test for a trivial center requires the promise that any nontrivial center has at least a stated minimum dimension.
paper_structure: The paper moves from the general theory of radical finding via kernel projection to the specific implementation for compact algebras, deriving structural theorems regarding the condition number and culminating in a test for the triviality of the center.
why_interesting: It directly addresses the mathematical structure of conserved quantities (the center/radical) in quantum dynamics, providing a quantum computational tool to diagnose internal symmetries in closed quantum systems.
